title: Supplemental Postoperative Oxygen and Wound Infection in Morbidly Obese Patients
brief_summary: The investigators propose to test the hypothesis that the incidence of major complications related to infection or inadequate healing is reduced in morbidly obese patients given 80% inspired oxygen during, and for 12-18 hours after, surgery compared with patients given 80% oxygen only during surgery. The primary outcome will be a composite of major complications plausibly related to infection or healing.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients with a BMI \> 35 kg/m2 undergoing open or laparoscopic gastric bypass

Exclusion Criteria:

* Surgeon does not anticipate primary wound closure
* History of fever or infection within 24 hours of surgery
* History of susceptibility to malignant hyperthermia
* Current heart or lung disease
